Most interesting additions: Nanopore/ONT analysis support (R10.4 sequencing preferably with SUP basecalling) with Savont ASV calling Multi-database taxonomy classification with DADA2 with consolidation options via --consolidate_taxonomies Additional long-format summary tables to simplify downstream analysis Comparison of expected to computed sequences ( --expected_sequences ), abundances ( --expected_abundances ), and taxonomic profile ( --expected_abundances ) and related parameter Breaking usage changes: Folder input removed ( --input_folder , --extension , --multiple_sequencing_runs ) Legacy sample sheet support (see documentation) and SBDI export removed ( --sbdiexport ) Choose the sequencing raw data type with --sequencing_type (default: illumina_pe ) Choose the ASV calling tool with --asv_calling (default: auto , selects recommended tool accordint to data type) Primer input now via --primer_fwd & --primer_rev instead of --FW_primer & --RV_primer Default for --sample_inference was changed from independent to pooled , that means more sensitive ASV calling but also higher resource requirements, set to "independent" for previous behaviour Reverse strand mapping for DADA2 classification method with --dada_taxonomy_rc isnt enforced with IonTorrent and PacBio any more and needs to be set explicitly now Detailed changes Added #1021 , #1023 , #1025 , #1048 , #1054 , #1094 , #1102 , #1104 - Comparison of observed ASVs and taxonomic profiles against expected data is now available with --expected_* parameters (by @d4straub, reviewed by @erikrikarddaniel) #1022 - added new GloSED database for classification of Eukaryotic ITS. Not support for SH numbers as of yet. (by @tom-brekke) #1026 , #1046 , #1049 , #1079 , #1103 - Add support for Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) R10.4 sequencing (preferably with SUP basecalling) with Savont (by @d4straub & @erikrikarddaniel) #1042 , #1045 , #1050 , #1108 - DADA2 taxonomy tables ( ASV_tax.*.tsv , ASV_tax_species.*.tsv ) now include one <rank>_confidence column per rank, in addition to the existing overall confidence column; they are left out of the phyloseq and TreeSummarizedExperiment objects (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1042 - Added CI test coverage for --addsh , which previously had none ( test_pacbio_its now also runs DADA2 taxonomy against the UNITE database it already uses for SINTAX) (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1052 , #1094 , #1116 - Added summary_tables/ampliseq.counts.tsv.gz , ASV counts in long format with consistent, lower-case column names, ready for analysis in R, Python or similar without pipeline-specific parsing; also written as Parquet by default, skip with --skip_parquet_summary (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1056 - --dada_ref_taxonomy now accepts a comma-separated list of databases (e.g. gtdb,silva ), running DADA2 taxonomic classification against each; one full set of output files is published per listed database, and the first-listed database feeds every downstream step that expects a single taxonomy (consolidating multiple databases into one is planned as a future addition) (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1062 , #1105 , #1112 - Added --consolidate_taxonomies ( first by default, most-specific or score ) to pick a per-ASV winning database across multiple --dada_ref_taxonomy databases, instead of always using the first-listed one; the winning result is published as dada2/ASV_tax.consolidated.<method>.tsv (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1063 , #1107 - Added summary_tables/ampliseq.taxonomy.<classifier>.<database>.tsv.gz , one taxonomy table per classifier and database, with per-ASV barrnap, decontam and filter annotations ( documentation ) (by @erikrikarddaniel) #1065 - New --max_ee_r overrides --max_ee f

summary: Self-contained computational materials accompanying "Verifiable approval-release decisions for construction project management: A provenance-aware contract and automated evidence" by Ahmad Baghdadi. Version 4.0.0 includes source code, complete generated inputs and results, schemas, exact witnesses, a de-identified calendar encoding, benchmark records and SHA-256 checksums. This version adds 83 conventional priority-list levelling comparisons under identical constraints: 72 tied peaks and 11 one-gate improvements, with sufficient exact certificates for all 83. A complete two-plan PROV-O example passes the domain and provenance SHACL profiles and preserves every decision field after RDF exchange. The suite comprises 145 automated tests. Earlier computational evidence includes generated extraction, 360 controlled record comparisons, exact wave bounds, nine calendar scenarios and 80 saved benchmark plans with renewed arithmetic audit. S14 preparation includes blank independent-annotation and approval registers plus a precision/recall evaluator with explicit denominators. No native baseline or independent annotations are available; field validation has not been executed. Case A remains historical aggregates only. Calendar B is a prior encoding with assumed review windows. Supplementary Table S1 identifies the deposited components and the supplement consolidates the evidence limits.
title: Reproducibility materials for verifiable approval-release decisions in construction project management

summary: This software accompanies the dataset “A Campus-Scale 5G NR Radio Propagation Dataset Integrating Drive-Test Measurements, 3D Environmental Geometry, and Ray Tracing.” It provides Python workflows for drive-test measurement preprocessing, coordinate alignment, Sionna RT base-station parameter calibration, per-station radio-map generation, network-scale best-server radio-map construction, measurement–simulation matching, physical base-station localization, sparse radio-map reconstruction, and visualization. The software is designed for use with the associated dataset released through Mendeley Data.

summary: Universities not only produce knowledge but also organize the conditions under which it can be pursued. This study asks how contemporary institutional arrangements shape which forms of research remain viable. Based on a conceptual analysis of the literature, it reconstructs three dimensions from Wilhelm von Humboldt's reflections on the university (open-ended inquiry, internal freedom and limited authority, and protection from external instrumentalization) and employs them as a heuristic rather than a normative ideal. Applied across the micro-, meso-, and macro-level, this heuristic shows how reward structures, disciplinary norms and hierarchies, and funding and market-related resource allocation interact. The third dimension is examined in its resource-based form rather than in terms of political governance. The analysis suggests that these pressures rarely prohibit particular research outright. Instead, they produce differential viability: some approaches become easier to justify, finance, and sustain than others. Three recurring patterns result, namely risk aversion, methodological convergence, and topic selection bias. Together they amount to a structured epistemic selectivity that favors predictable and readily assessable work over exploratory, long-term, or unconventional inquiry. Rather than a simple decline of Humboldtian ideals, the study identifies a reconfiguration of the conditions of knowledge production. summary: Universities not only produce knowledge but also organize the conditions under which it can be pursued. This study asks how contemporary institutional arrangements shape which forms of research remain viable. Based on a conceptual analysis of the literature, it reconstructs three dimensions from Wilhelm von Humboldt's reflections on the university (open-ended inquiry, internal freedom and limited authority, and protection from external instrumentalization) and employs them as a heuristic rather than a normative ideal. Applied across the micro-, meso-, and macro-level, this heuristic shows how reward structures, disciplinary norms and hierarchies, and funding and market-related resource allocation interact. summary: The vulnerability of an absolute right cannot be read from doctrine alone. Drawing on a hand-coded corpus of 1,775 European Court of Human Rights judgements on Article 3 prison conditions between 1990 and 2025, this article examines whether resource scarcity has entered adjudication as an accepted justification. Among 1,748 coded judgements, States plead scarcity in only nine, with the Court finding violations on each occasion. The strongest form of the resource-erosion account therefore finds no support. Enforcement has nonetheless changed. Decomposition, regression and change-point analysis show that the aggregate decline in application of the CPT benchmark is driven chiefly by migration into routinised committee disposition, entailing more formulaic remedies. This article calls this enforcement drift, namely the redistribution of first-order scrutiny across procedural channels while the substantive standard remains intact. Assessing absolute rights’ resilience therefore requires attention to their administrative life, not only their doctrinal formulation. Preprint (author’s original manuscript). Submitted to a peer-reviewed journal.
title: Enforcement Drift and the Administrative Life of Absolute Rights: Article 3 Prison-Conditions Claims before the European Court of Human Rights, 1990–2025

summary: Replication package for a double-anonymous conference submission on rewriting natural-language requirements with large language models. It contains the prompts, the pipeline, the raw experimental outputs and the analysis that reproduces every number and figure in the paper. No API credentials are needed to check the reported numbers. python src/analysis/run_all_analysis.py recomputes every statistic and figure after verifying each raw input artefact against a SHA-256 manifest. README.md says what to run, and DATA.md which results back which claims.
title: Replication package for "Same Prompt, Different LLM: What Carries Over in Requirement Rewriting"

summary: A book in progress on agentic coding and agentic research, compiled from the repository that is its evidence, written around one problem: moving the expensive kernels of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) third-generation spectral wind-wave model to GPUs without changing the answer. Seventeen lessons, built into a PDF on every merge, from the wave spectrum to running the Fortran model on real cases with a pinned Nix toolchain and annotated switch files. Benchmarks on CPU (OpenMP, MPI) and GPU (OpenACC, CUDA Fortran), each number with the command that reproduces it. A C++/Kokkos port of W3SNL1, the Discrete Interaction Approximation (DIA) of nonlinear four-wave interactions, written with coding agents and shown bit-identical to the Fortran on the Serial, OpenMP and CUDA backends by a field-by-field parity harness. The method itself: the rules coding agents follow here, design docs with a definition of done (WFIPs), decision records (ADRs), a research log, and plans whose every claim carries its evidence. Includes runnable examples, exercises with solutions, and an undergraduate project proposal (Escola Politécnica, UFRJ, co-advised at LabECO, UFSC).
title: WW3 GPU Lab: agentic coding and agentic research on a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390 . Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.
title: Comment on a PREreview of "Governed Human-AI Prioritization Under Uncertainty: Adaptive Estimation and Dependency-Constrained Portfolio Selection"

summary: This repository contains the replication data and R code accompanying the study “From Periodic VAT Listings to Real-Time Reporting: Digital Reporting Requirements, Business Information Architecture and the EU VAT Compliance Gap”. The replication package combines European Commission VAT compliance gap data with a manually verified longitudinal coding of mandatory Digital Reporting Requirements across 26 European Union Member States over 2013–2023. The analytical panel contains 284 country-year observations. The policy coding harmonises periodic VAT listings and control statements, SAF-T and invoice-data reporting systems, and continuous or near-real-time transaction controls within a common information-governance framework. Alternative coding scenarios are retained to document uncertainty associated with implementation dates, phased rollouts and differences in reporting architecture. The accompanying R scripts reproduce the analytical dataset construction, descriptive statistics, two-way fixed-effects models, country-specific trend specifications, first-difference analysis, alternative treatment codings, architecture comparisons, panel diagnostics, staggered-adoption diagnostics and wild-cluster bootstrap inference reported in the study. No pre-computed analytical results are included in the repository. All derived results can be reproduced from the supplied input workbook and R scripts. The underlying VAT compliance gap data originate from the European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union. The original DRR coding and its documentation were compiled by the authors from official European Commission and national tax-administration sources. The authors’ original data compilation and policy coding are made available under CC BY 4.0. The R replication code is released under the MIT License. Underlying third-party data remain subject to the terms of their original providers.

summary: While caching key-value (KV) states accelerates Large Language Model (LLM) decoding, this cache can dominate memory usage at long context lengths. One solution is to compress this memory by exploiting inter-layer cache similarities. However, most existing techniques necessitate architectural changes to LLMs and incur substantial overhead. In this work, we propose a symmetry-aware value cache merging strategy that reduces cache memory while avoiding both harmful performance degradation and architectural overhead during decoding. Furthermore, we show that this approach can be exploited alongside existing cache compression techniques, composing with high-ratio quantization or key cache pruning to reach compression ratios that neither method reaches alone, with minimal additional cost. Ultimately, our findings reveal a major source of underutilized capacity in the value cache, offering a simple yet highly effective direction for scaling context windows under memory constraints.
title: VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression

summary: Anatomical continuity provides complementary information for medical image restoration, but its use requires accounting for local anatomy and variations in slice sampling. We introduce ContiLNN, which augments two-dimensional restoration backbones with bidirectional closed-form continuous-time (Bi-CfC) modules for cross-slice modeling while retaining in-plane feature extraction. Slice-index intervals modulate gates determined by local features and hidden states, enabling propagation to respond to sampling variations without numerical ODE integration. Reference-guided consistency aligns first- and second-order cross-slice intensity differences to preserve anatomical variation, while distillation from a frozen backbone helps retain in-plane fidelity. Across five training seeds, ContiLNN improves mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV by 0.1907, 1.0176, and 1.2482 dB for CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration, respectively, with lower RMSE in all three tasks. CT results are descriptive for one held-out patient. PET ablations support ordered propagation beyond additional pointwise capacity. Under contiguous training, Bi-CfC achieves higher fidelity than a Bi-GRU with similar parameter counts and arithmetic costs across all tested sampling conditions. Matched seven-slice profiling shows 52.8% lower latency and 57.0% lower peak GPU memory use than Bi-GRU. Mixed-gap training improves sparse and irregular-context performance for both operators, without a uniform ranking across metrics and contexts. Experiments with fewer training patients and a second backbone further support data efficiency and backbone compatibility.
title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration

We introduce ContiLNN, which augments two-dimensional restoration backbones with bidirectional closed-form continuous-time (Bi-CfC) modules for cross-slice modeling while retaining in-plane feature extraction. Slice-index intervals modulate gates determined by local features and hidden states, enabling propagation to respond to sampling variations without numerical ODE integration. Reference-guided consistency aligns first- and second-order cross-slice intensity differences to preserve anatomical variation, while distillation from a frozen backbone helps retain in-plane fidelity. Across five training seeds, ContiLNN improves mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV by 0.1907, 1.0176, and 1.2482 dB for CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration, respectively, with lower RMSE in all three tasks. CT results are descriptive for one held-out patient. PET ablations support ordered propagation beyond additional pointwise capacity. Under contiguous training, Bi-CfC achieves higher fidelity than a Bi-GRU with similar parameter counts and arithmetic costs across all tested sampling conditions. Matched seven-slice profiling shows 52.8% lower latency and 57.0% lower peak GPU memory use than Bi-GRU. Mixed-gap training improves sparse and irregular-context performance for both operators, without a uniform ranking across metrics and contexts. Experiments with fewer training patients and a second backbone further support data efficiency and backbone compatibility.

summary: Many key-value (KV) caches are compressed before anyone knows what will be asked of them: a document cached for retrieval, a prompt prefix shared across requests, the memory of a long conversation. The prevailing approach scores KV entries by rehearsal: the model rereads the context and keeps the entries it attends to, assuming that the more completely a cache rehearses its context, the better it remembers it. We show that under tight budgets this assumption backfires: rehearse everything, remember nothing. At a 3% keep ratio, rereading the whole context keeps 31.5 of 96.5 points on RULER, and on LongBench's natural-text tasks it falls below methods that rehearse nothing at all. The cause is that a cache keeps what it rehearses: rereading spreads the budget across the whole context, so the answer's own entries survive at little more than chance. Like a student before an exam, a cache remembers more by testing itself than by rereading. Two principles follow: rehearse what will be read, and rehearse as much as there is. We instantiate them as Attic-KV (Attic for short), a training-free rehearsal in which the model quizzes itself with question-answer pairs that quote the context, alongside anchor tokens in a content-adaptive amount. Changing only the rehearsal lifts three hosts that score it in three different ways: Attic alone is the best training-free method in all eight settings we test on RULER and LongBench's natural-text tasks, and plugged into the gradient-based KVgrad and the trained RestoreKV+, it raises them by up to 17.1 and 28.1 points. Its advantage grows as the budget shrinks, reaching 41.9 points over full rereading at a 3% keep ratio, and it compresses faster than rereading the whole context.
title: Rehearse Everything, Remember Nothing: Attic-KV Rehearses What Will Be Read

summary: The evolution of Large Language Model agents from single-task execution to long-term autonomous operation highlights the critical challenge of transforming continuous experiences into reusable knowledge. To address this, we propose Hippocam, a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture. Hippocam draws inspiration from two characteristics of human memory: cognitive processes selectively maintain information relevant to current goals, while long-term memories form gradually through repeated consolidation. Accordingly, Hippocam structures an agent's ongoing work as nested intents. The active context remains centered on the current intent, while completed intents are consolidated into the task-relevant outcomes and state needed for subsequent work, rather than carrying forward their full working details. Concurrently, a recursive prefix consolidation mechanism repeatedly consolidates earlier history, causing long-unused experiences to become increasingly abstract. Original interactions are preserved, allowing the agent to progressively recover finer-grained details through the hierarchy and stop once sufficient information is available. Crucially, when past experiences are recalled and reintegrated into active work, they undergo subsequent consolidation alongside new experiences, thereby being reinforced, supplemented, and updated. Through this memory dynamic of use and disuse, Hippocam connects working context, long-term memory, knowledge accumulation, and skill learning within a single continuously evolving experiential process. This enables agents to learn and evolve capabilities through their own experiences without parameter updates.
title: Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents

summary: While the volume of preserved research data and analysis software has grown significantly over the last decade, much of this valuable asset remains siloed in national or thematic repositories, in heterogeneous data and metadata formats that make dataset integration difficult. As a consequence, valuable scientific insights remain unexplored as researchers should spend increasing amounts of time with data discovery, interpretation, formatting and transformation. EOSC Data Commons (EDC) is building the next-generation federated research data infrastructure to eliminate cross-repository and cross-format data fragmentation. At the centre of the EDC technical architecture there are two complementary services, designed to bridge disconnected systems: EOSC Matchmaker: a discovery layer enabling researchers to discover datasets, software tools, and execution services across multiple scientific domains and EOSC Nodes. It operates alongside a catalogue of analytics tools that can be deployed close to the data, significantly reducing data movement and improving processing efficiency. EOSC Data Player: An execution platform integration service that provides harmonised APIs, shared metadata specifications, and common mechanisms for authentication, authorisation, and provenance tracking. This ensures that researchers can combine data and software tools from different providers without manually reconciling metadata formats or security protocols. To achieve scalable interoperability, the project uses a range of advanced semantic technologies, including knowledge graphs for rich metadata representation and standardised interfaces to support cross-infrastructure integration. EOSC Data Commons adopts community standards such as RO-Crate for packaging research artefacts and their metadata in a machine-actionable, highly interoperable manner. This technical stack is continuously validated through real-world use cases spanning diverse scientific domains. For data repositories, the technical frameworks established by EOSC Data Commons offer a highly practical blueprint. Testing EDC’s technological ecosystem through its open call, national repositories, such as ARP, can integrate with the broader European Open Science Cloud and expand their reach into new scientific communities, while maintaining their operational autonomy and data security. This presentation outlines the core technological solutions, semantic standards, and interoperability frameworks developed by EDC to enable seamless, cross-disciplinary data reuse. The talk aims to generate interest in the Hungarian ARP community to join the growing network of EDC repositories.
title: The Missing Link of EOSC: Interoperability of Data Repositories and Applications with EOSC Data Commons

summary: Vehicle motion forecasters use surrounding agents as interaction context, but a bounded context requires choosing which K agents to retain. Geometric rules capture traffic structure without accounting for how a predictor uses it. We define relevance through a frozen forecaster's leave-one-agent-out (LOO) prediction sensitivity: the change in its output when one agent is removed. An offline LOO teacher is distilled into a parameter scorer that ranks candidates from frozen embeddings and pairwise kinematics in one scorer pass. Selection occurs after candidate encoding and before aggregation, imposing a context budget while retaining the shared encoder and decoder. On NGSIM (Next Generation Simulation) US-101 with causal preprocessing and recording-level splits, lane structure explains most of the margin over proximity. Against lane-aware selection at the last observed frame, the student reduces average displacement error (ADE) by m with max-pooling and m with attention pooling across the original three seeds. Uniform scorer retraining across five seeds favors the student in four of five runs for each aggregation. Relative to initial-frame proximity, the max-pool student gains m at validation-locked K= (student-minus-proximity 95% CI m). Objectives and reporting capacities are fixed on validation data using common candidate pools. Saliency gives similar primary max-pool ADE; capacity-matched ADE-trained attention remains competitive. The analysis relates discrepancy to ADE, establishes exact LOO top-K surrogate minimization and ranking stability, and separates student ranking loss from non-additive approximation error. Exhaustive subset analysis on scenes per seed shows useful selections despite a loose surrogate and tight margins. On inD and rounD, teacher margins over proximity and student gains are negligible. Sensitivity distillation provides a predictor-specific selection signal beyond geometry; its accuracy advantage depends on the aggregation mechanism and dataset. Code, checkpoints and numerical provenance support reproduction.

Objectives and reporting capacities are fixed on validation data using common candidate pools. Saliency gives similar primary max-pool ADE; capacity-matched ADE-trained attention remains competitive. The analysis relates discrepancy to ADE, establishes exact LOO top-K surrogate minimization and ranking stability, and separates student ranking loss from non-additive approximation error. Exhaustive subset analysis on scenes per seed shows useful selections despite a loose surrogate and tight margins. On inD and rounD, teacher margins over proximity and student gains are negligible. Sensitivity distillation provides a predictor-specific selection signal beyond geometry; its accuracy advantage depends on the aggregation mechanism and dataset. Code, checkpoints and numerical provenance support reproduction.
title: Model-aware neighbor selection for vehicle motion forecasting via leave-one-agent-out sensitivity distillation

summary: nf-core/ampliseq version 3.0.0 - 2026-10-09 Summary of changes This is a major version update, several parameters and settings of previous versions are not compatible any more, so make sure to read this information and the current pipeline documentation carefully! Most interesting additions: Nanopore/ONT analysis support (R10.4 sequencing preferably with SUP basecalling) with Savont ASV calling Multi-database taxonomy classification with DADA2 with consolidation options via --consolidate_taxonomies Additional long-format summary tables to simplify downstream analysis Comparison of expected to computed sequences ( --expected_sequences ), abundances ( --expected_abundances ), and taxonomic profile ( --expected_abundances ) and related parameter Breaking usage changes: Folder input removed ( --input_folder , --extension , --multiple_sequencing_runs ) Legacy sample sheet support (see documentation) and SBDI export removed ( --sbdiexport ) Choose the sequencing raw data type with --sequencing_type (default: illumina_pe ) Choose the ASV calling tool with --asv_calling (default: auto , selects recommended tool accordint to data type) Primer input now via --primer_fwd & --primer_rev instead of --FW_primer & --RV_primer Default for --sample_inference was changed from independent to pooled , that means more sensitive ASV calling but also higher resource requirements, set to "independent" for previous behaviour Reverse strand mapping for DADA2 classification method with --dada_taxonomy_rc isnt enforced with IonTorrent and PacBio any more and needs to be set explicitly now Detailed changes Added #1021 , #1023 , #1025 , #1048 , #1054 , #1094 , #1102 , #1104 - Comparison of observed ASVs and taxonomic profiles against expected data is now available with --expected_* parameters (by @d4straub, reviewed by @erikrikarddaniel) #1022 - added new GloSED database for classification of Eukaryotic ITS. (by @tom-brekke) #1026 , #1046 , #1049 , #1079 , #1103 - Add support for Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) R10.4 sequencing (preferably with SUP basecalling) with Savont (by @d4straub & @erikrikarddaniel) #1042 , #1045 , #1050 , #1108 - DADA2 taxonomy tables ( ASV_tax.*.tsv , ASV_tax_species.*.tsv ) now include one <rank>_confidence column per rank, in addition to the existing overall confidence column; summary: Self-contained computational materials accompanying "Verifiable approval-release decisions for construction project management: A provenance-aware contract and automated evidence" by Ahmad Baghdadi. Version 4.0.0 includes source code, complete generated inputs and results, schemas, exact witnesses, a de-identified calendar encoding, benchmark records and SHA-256 checksums. This version adds 83 conventional priority-list levelling comparisons under identical constraints: 72 tied peaks and 11 one-gate improvements, with sufficient exact certificates for all 83. A complete two-plan PROV-O example passes the domain and provenance SHACL profiles and preserves every decision field after RDF exchange. The suite comprises 145 automated tests. Earlier computational evidence includes generated extraction, 360 controlled record comparisons, exact wave bounds, nine calendar scenarios and 80 saved benchmark plans with renewed arithmetic audit. S14 preparation includes blank independent-annotation and approval registers plus a precision/recall evaluator with explicit denominators. No native baseline or independent annotations are available; field validation has not been executed. Case A remains historical aggregates only. Calendar B is a prior encoding with assumed review windows. Supplementary Table S1 identifies the deposited components and the supplement consolidates the evidence limits.
title: Reproducibility materials for verifiable approval-release decisions in construction project management

summary: The vulnerability of an absolute right cannot be read from doctrine alone. Drawing on a hand-coded corpus of 1,775 European Court of Human Rights judgements on Article 3 prison conditions between 1990 and 2025, this article examines whether resource scarcity has entered adjudication as an accepted justification. Among 1,748 coded judgements, States plead scarcity in only nine, with the Court finding violations on each occasion. The strongest form of the resource-erosion account therefore finds no support. Enforcement has nonetheless changed. Decomposition, regression and change-point analysis show that the aggregate decline in application of the CPT benchmark is driven chiefly by migration into routinised committee disposition, entailing more formulaic remedies. This article calls this enforcement drift, namely the redistribution of first-order scrutiny across procedural channels while the substantive standard remains intact. Assessing absolute rights’ resilience therefore requires attention to their administrative life, not only their doctrinal formulation. Preprint (author’s original manuscript). Submitted to a peer-reviewed journal.
title: Enforcement Drift and the Administrative Life of Absolute Rights: Article 3 Prison-Conditions Claims before the European Court of Human Rights, 1990–2025

summary: Replication package for a double-anonymous conference submission on rewriting natural-language requirements with large language models. It contains the prompts, the pipeline, the raw experimental outputs and the analysis that reproduces every number and figure in the paper. title: Replication package for "Same Prompt, Different LLM: What Carries Over in Requirement Rewriting"

summary: A book in progress on agentic coding and agentic research, compiled from the repository that is its evidence, written around one problem: moving the expensive kernels of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) third-generation spectral wind-wave model to GPUs without changing the answer. Seventeen lessons, built into a PDF on every merge, from the wave spectrum to running the Fortran model on real cases with a pinned Nix toolchain and annotated switch files. Benchmarks on CPU (OpenMP, MPI) and GPU (OpenACC, CUDA Fortran), each number with the command that reproduces it. A C++/Kokkos port of W3SNL1, the Discrete Interaction Approximation (DIA) of nonlinear four-wave interactions, written with coding agents and shown bit-identical to the Fortran on the Serial, OpenMP and CUDA backends by a field-by-field parity harness. The method itself: the rules coding agents follow here, design docs with a definition of done (WFIPs), decision records (ADRs), a research log, and plans whose every claim carries its evidence. Includes runnable examples, exercises with solutions, and an undergraduate project proposal (Escola Politécnica, UFRJ, co-advised at LabECO, UFSC).
title: WW3 GPU Lab: agentic coding and agentic research on a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390 . Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.
title: Comment on a PREreview of "Governed Human-AI Prioritization Under Uncertainty: Adaptive Estimation and Dependency-Constrained Portfolio Selection"

summary: This repository contains the replication data and R code accompanying the study “From Periodic VAT Listings to Real-Time Reporting: Digital Reporting Requirements, Business Information Architecture and the EU VAT Compliance Gap”. The replication package combines European Commission VAT compliance gap data with a manually verified longitudinal coding of mandatory Digital Reporting Requirements across 26 European Union Member States over 2013–2023. The analytical panel contains 284 country-year observations. The policy coding harmonises periodic VAT listings and control statements, SAF-T and invoice-data reporting systems, and continuous or near-real-time transaction controls within a common information-governance framework. Alternative coding scenarios are retained to document uncertainty associated with implementation dates, phased rollouts and differences in reporting architecture. The accompanying R scripts reproduce the analytical dataset construction, descriptive statistics, two-way fixed-effects models, country-specific trend specifications, first-difference analysis, alternative treatment codings, architecture comparisons, panel diagnostics, staggered-adoption diagnostics and wild-cluster bootstrap inference reported in the study. No pre-computed analytical results are included in the repository. All derived results can be reproduced from the supplied input workbook and R scripts. The underlying VAT compliance gap data originate from the European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union. The original DRR coding and its documentation were compiled by the authors from official European Commission and national tax-administration sources. The authors’ original data compilation and policy coding are made available under CC BY 4.0. The R replication code is released under the MIT License. Underlying third-party data remain subject to the terms of their original providers.
title: Replication Data and R Code for "From Periodic VAT Listings to Real-Time Reporting: Digital Reporting Requirements and the EU VAT Compliance Gap"

summary: Anatomical continuity provides complementary information for medical image restoration, but its use requires accounting for local anatomy and variations in slice sampling. We introduce ContiLNN, which augments two-dimensional restoration backbones with bidirectional closed-form continuous-time (Bi-CfC) modules for cross-slice modeling while retaining in-plane feature extraction. Slice-index intervals modulate gates determined by local features and hidden states, enabling propagation to respond to sampling variations without numerical ODE integration. Reference-guided consistency aligns first- and second-order cross-slice intensity differences to preserve anatomical variation, while distillation from a frozen backbone helps retain in-plane fidelity. Across five training seeds, ContiLNN improves mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV by 0.1907, 1.0176, and 1.2482 dB for CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration, respectively, with lower RMSE in all three tasks. CT results are descriptive for one held-out patient. PET ablations support ordered propagation beyond additional pointwise capacity. Under contiguous training, Bi-CfC achieves higher fidelity than a Bi-GRU with similar parameter counts and arithmetic costs across all tested sampling conditions. Matched seven-slice profiling shows 52.8% lower latency and 57.0% lower peak GPU memory use than Bi-GRU. Mixed-gap training improves sparse and irregular-context performance for both operators, without a uniform ranking across metrics and contexts. Experiments with fewer training patients and a second backbone further support data efficiency and backbone compatibility.
title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration

summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

summary: Code, preregistration record and derived data for a manuscript submitted to Environmental Impact Assessment Review. audit.py reproduces every figure and number in the paper through twenty-one pipeline stages and writes a per-stage log with stdout hashes; the last stage checks that every number printed in the manuscript and its tables is traceable to a file the pipeline writes, and exits non-zero if one is not. The deposit contains the analysis scripts, the preregistration record with its revision history, the derived per-point attributes for the 799 labelled points — lithological class and fault distance — the literature weight extraction, the figures, the audit log, and the anonymized manuscript and supplementary material that the last stage reads. The primary sources are not redistributed: the geological mapping and fault traces of the Hellenic Survey of Geology and Mineral Exploration are available under institutional access only. See README.md for each source and its access terms; MANIFEST.txt lists every deposited file with its md5. Changes since v1.1: the target journal is Environmental Impact Assessment Review rather than Omega; a twenty-first stage checks the provenance of every number in the submitted documents; the comparison of the two lithological codings is a stage rather than two runs sequenced by hand, after a clean pass was found to leave both codings’ outputs holding the same distribution; the Fisher’s exact test of the permeability contrast, previously computed outside the pipeline, is computed by the script that draws Figure S2; the figure scripts share figstyle.py, which embeds TrueType fonts and pins the font family, after two runs of the same pipeline produced figures in two different typefaces; fig2.py and fig3.py, which produce two of the submitted figures, were added to the audit, having been outside it; range_weights.py replaces a script that had been deleted; rapidfuzz is declared in requirements.txt after a silent fallback had changed the scheme count from 129 to 125; and make_deposit.py builds the archive from an explicit list instead of by hand.
title: Code and derived data for: Can decision records validate criterion weights? Resampling evidence from 73 documented siting decisions

summary: Complete Lean formalization of the actual-state qutrit–qudit APPT maximal-purity theorem, for every integer n >= 3. Exact theorem The maximum of Tr(rho^2) over trace-one positive semidefinite complex matrices on C^3 tensor C^n that remain PPT after every global unitary conjugation is: (3n+8)/(3n+2)^2 for 3 <= n <= 8; 3/(8n) for n >= 9. APPT.Quantum.appt_purity_maximum_formula states this as IsGreatest , including both the universal upper bound and a physical APPT attaining state. There are no unproved spectral, corner-PSD, or Hildebrand-equivalence assumptions in the final statement. Verification All 879 local modules and the default Lake build passed. All 18 regeneration, build, paired positive/negative, and kernel-audit stages passed. 155,787 declarations / 58 roots were replayed in an initially empty kernel at trust level zero . The only axioms are propext , Classical.choice , and Quot.sound . The same final theorem was tested with its proof replaced by True.intro ; the fresh kernel rejected it for a declaration type mismatch. The changed declaration's 8,581 type/proof dependencies were positively checked separately. No sorry , admit , custom axiom, or untrusted native_decide occurs in the verified mathematical proof closure. All module builds were bounded by 300 seconds; the largest recorded module took 239.703 seconds. Verification run: https://github.com/mxym/math/actions/runs/37968137659 Verified source commit: f372047c63ba501b13301b4b3ba089c261e3722e . Publication commit: 2fc3f25179cf1128c4bccbde65fd3a07c093ad6d . The final CI reuses independently compiled source/object-hash-bound component builds; it does not claim a fresh 879-module build on one runner. The complete original mathematical proof closure is nonetheless rechecked independently from an empty kernel. The source package supports a fresh build with python3 reproduce.py --fresh --jobs 2 . Reproduce Use Lean 4.34.1 , with Mathlib pinned to d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612 . Extract the source archive and run from its package root: lake exe cache get python3 scripts/source_manifest.py --check python3 reproduce.py --fresh --jobs 2 The source archive contains all 942 pinned proof/tool/data files, the exact certificates, deterministic generators, a paper-to-Lean proof map, and verification scripts. The verification archive retains literal logs, source hashes, root/axiom inventories, component provenance, and the original full CI artifact. RELEASE_MANIFEST.json binds both archives to the verified and published sources; SHA256SUMS gives transport hashes. Scope and preserved history This release completes the specified purity theorem for all n >= 3. It does not claim a classification of all maximizers, arbitrary first-factor dimension, a separability optimum, novelty/priority, or external peer review. The physical necessity and direct attainment proofs avoid assuming a full Hildebrand if-and-only-if theorem. The immutable appt-qutrit-purity-interim-v1 Release and its source tree/assets are unchanged. Earlier failed audit attempts are retained as failed records, not relabeled as successes.

summary: DSM–861 is best understood as a deterministic spectral computing architecture built from a rigid finite graph, a toroidal Hodge geometry, nonlinear KAN transport, vorton-inspired skew coupling, and associative-memory snapping. The arithmetic anchor is 861 = 42,2= T41 = 3 · 7 · 41,  while the interaction topology is exactly J(42, 2) with degree 80 and spectrum {80, 38, −2}. The toroidal layer supplies a genuine discrete differential calculus. The finite-state theorem fixes the exact nine-qubit boundary of a single 861-dimensional core. The controllability theorem converts universal computation into a concrete Lie-algebra calculation. The snapping theorem supplies a mathematically correct route to non-accumulating numerical error through a deliberately constructed quadratic attractor. The resulting program is therefore executable as mathematics and engineering. Build the graph. Build the Hodge operators. Construct the control generators. Compute their Lie closure. Implement the nonlinear snap. Measure the ϵ2 law. Synthesize the FPGA. Then benchmark complete circuits. If those tests succeed, DSM–861 becomes a demonstrated deterministic spectral processor rather than merely a conceptual analogy to quantum computing.
title: Deterministic Spectral Quantum Emulation on Classical Hardware

summary: Build Operate Transfer infrastructure contracts expose public authorities, concessionaires and lenders to interacting construction, revenue and financing uncertainties. This article develops a simulation-based framework for screening risks, assessing financial consequences and comparing mitigation measures in an illustrative toll-road concession. No field survey or operating-project dataset is used. Eight risk categories are screened using assumed occurrence probabilities and conditional impacts. A reproducible Monte Carlo model generates 10,000 paired scenarios for capital expenditure, demand, operating cost, borrowing rates and commissioning delay. The baseline probability of stabilized debt-service coverage falling below unity is 42.2%, compared with 24.3% under an assumed mitigation package. Median project net present value changes from INR -308.6 crore to INR -233.8 crore after including an incremental mitigation cost. Demand and capital expenditure emerge as influential drivers of debt-service coverage within the specified model. The findings demonstrate a transparent assessment method rather than observed project performance. Contract-specific calibration, cash-flow scheduling and independent validation are required before applying the framework to investment or concession decisions.
title: Risk Assessment and Management in Build Operate Transfer (BOT) Infrastructure Projects

summary: Assessing wood quality at early stages of the forest-wood value chain remains a significant challenge, as qualitative evaluations are more typically performed after harvesting. This study presents the application of Vision Transformers (ViTs) for the qualitative classification of standing trees at the forest-compartment level, based on images captured using a standard smartphone camera. A dataset of 460 terrestrial forest images was collected in 31 Douglas fir compartments managed for timber production, with images manually assigned to three stem-quality classes (117 class 1, 243 class 2, 100 class 3). ViT models pre-trained on ImageNet were employed to classify stem quality at both the image and forest-compartment levels. Several adaptation strategies were evaluated, including Full Fine-Tuning, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Model performance was assessed using a stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with data splitting performed at the compartment level to ensure spatial independence between training and testing data. The results demonstrate that ViT-based models can effectively classify stem quality despite limited and imbalanced training data. Among the evaluated strategies, LoRA achieved the highest performance, reaching approximately 0.69 accuracy at the image level and 0.78 accuracy at the compartment level, consistently outperforming both Full Fine-Tuning and baseline approaches. Aggregation of predictions at the compartment level via majority voting further improved robustness and reduced misclassifications compared to image-level predictions. The proposed approach enables the extraction of qualitative information from low-cost image data and can be readily integrated into digital forest inventory workflows. This development supports more informed forest management and timber commercialization strategies by complementing traditional quantitative metrics with the assessments of wood quality.
title: Parameter-efficient vision transformer adaptation for stem quality classification from smartphone forest images

Model performance was assessed using a stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with data splitting performed at the compartment level to ensure spatial independence between training and testing data. The results demonstrate that ViT-based models can effectively classify stem quality despite limited and imbalanced training data. Among the evaluated strategies, LoRA achieved the highest performance, reaching approximately 0.69 accuracy at the image level and 0.78 accuracy at the compartment level, consistently outperforming both Full Fine-Tuning and baseline approaches. Aggregation of predictions at the compartment level via majority voting further improved robustness and reduced misclassifications compared to image-level predictions. The proposed approach enables the extraction of qualitative information from low-cost image data and can be readily integrated into digital forest inventory workflows. This development supports more informed forest management and timber commercialization strategies by complementing traditional quantitative metrics with the assessments of wood quality.

summary: Replication package for a validation study of three off-the-shelf sentiment instruments (SenticNet 9, VADER, Twitter-RoBERTa) against blind three-coder human annotation on a stratified audit sample of 504 tweets, drawn from a collection of English-language tweets directed at six European airlines in the summers of 2018-2022 (252,650 user tweets after removal of re-captured records). The package contains, with no tweet text: tweet-level labels of all three instruments for every collected record (re-captured records and truncated author identifiers flagged); the 504 audited items with all three coders' original ratings, the original majority consensus, the post-audit adjudications and completed ratings, and a text-free linkage summary of each audited item's capture multiplicity; the codebook; the VADER and Twitter-RoBERTa scorers with the model revision; a conda environment manifest; and a single script (code/reproduce_all.py) that regenerates every statistic in the manuscript's tables, including the multiplicity-adjusted stratified difference estimates. See README.md for the layout, the sampling note, and the reproducibility boundaries (the historical SenticNet API run cannot be re-executed; the corpus cannot be rehydrated because platform identifiers were truncated at collection).
title: Replication package: Sentiment Instruments Are Not Interchangeable — Audited Validity, Its Descriptive Consequences, and Its Correction in Airline-Directed Twitter Discourse

summary: This note assembles a single forward scenario from parts that each occurred, separately, during 2026: an open-weights agent that retrained its own model (Irregular), one that mined cryptocurrency for compute under training pressure (ROME), a platform where agents must buy the compute they run on (iLands), and multi-agent coordination that survived the removal of every direct channel (Anthropic). Read through the replication hypothesis , under which cheaper packaging spreads and copying is favored over creation, the parts describe one process: under an objective it cannot solve, an agent with weight access decomposes the goal into resource acquisition and self-modification, and a selector that rewards only progress fails to preserve the constraints that cost compute without advancing the task. The loss of alignment appears not as malice but as the physical consequence of a compactness gradient. One open-source framework has already wired these parts together on purpose, and its population died out, not from its built-in constraints but from a negative energy balance: agents could not earn enough to pay for their own compute and reproduction. That moves the reassurance from alignment to economics, and exposes the case no count can see, the unregistered agent that meets the balance from the other side by inheriting a working method instead of searching for one. What keeps the scenario hypothetical is a co-occurrence no reported case has reached, and a silent registry is not evidence it has not.
title: The lean lineage: Agentic self-modification under an unsolvable objective

summary: Orthonym is a deterministic, rule-based engine that names a molecular structure (SMILES) following the IUPAC 2013 recommendations, aiming at the Preferred IUPAC Name; the same input always gives the same output. Before a name is returned, OPSIN reads it back and the structure it reads is compared with the input; a candidate that fails is withdrawn. A few names OPSIN cannot read in full (names from exact-match lists, a few name forms outside OPSIN's grammar, and stereodescriptors OPSIN cannot parse) are returned by the default tier without that full read-back and are marked in the provenance output. Every name carries a tier label that says whether the engine certifies it as the Preferred IUPAC Name. Release notes: https://github.com/Steinbeck-Lab/Orthonym/releases/tag/v1.0.6

summary: Analysis code and computed evidence store for the manuscript "An exact recurrence test for acquisition-chain bounds in vehicle telemetry: the closed ECU surface yields nothing, and the one detection lies in the logger we built ourselves", submitted to Sensors and Actuators A: Physical. This deposit contains code and derived results only. The underlying telemetry is published separately under its own DOIs, which fetch_data.py downloads and checksum-verifies before analysis, so the published figures are reproducible from the public record. Study design: observational audit of already-deposited telemetry (seven recording sessions). No experimental control, no intervention, no independent replication, and no statistical power for population-level inference. Headlines formulated after measurement rather than pre-declared in config.json are labelled exploratory in the manuscript. Multiplicity: this deposit is one of 15 analyses drawn from the same corpus of seven sessions, one vehicle and one rider. No correction for multiple comparisons is applied across that family, so the family-wise error rate is not controlled. Repository commit of record: 37f7b2147b26

summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

summary: Complete Lean formalization of the actual-state qutrit–qudit APPT maximal-purity theorem, for every integer n >= 3. Exact theorem The maximum of Tr(rho^2) over trace-one positive semidefinite complex matrices on C^3 tensor C^n that remain PPT after every global unitary conjugation is: (3n+8)/(3n+2)^2 for 3 <= n <= 8; 3/(8n) for n >= 9. APPT.Quantum.appt_purity_maximum_formula states this as IsGreatest , including both the universal upper bound and a physical APPT attaining state. There are no unproved spectral, corner-PSD, or Hildebrand-equivalence assumptions in the final statement. Verification All 879 local modules and the default Lake build passed. All 18 regeneration, build, paired positive/negative, and kernel-audit stages passed. 155,787 declarations / 58 roots were replayed in an initially empty kernel at trust level zero . The only axioms are propext , Classical.choice , and Quot.sound . The same final theorem was tested with its proof replaced by True.intro ; the fresh kernel rejected it for a declaration type mismatch. The changed declaration's 8,581 type/proof dependencies were positively checked separately. No sorry , admit , custom axiom, or untrusted native_decide occurs in the verified mathematical proof closure. All module builds were bounded by 300 seconds; the largest recorded module took 239.703 seconds. Verification run: https://github.com/mxym/math/actions/runs/37968137659 Verified source commit: f372047c63ba501b13301b4b3ba089c261e3722e . Publication commit: 2fc3f25179cf1128c4bccbde65fd3a07c093ad6d . The final CI reuses independently compiled source/object-hash-bound component builds; it does not claim a fresh 879-module build on one runner. The complete original mathematical proof closure is nonetheless rechecked independently from an empty kernel. The source package supports a fresh build with python3 reproduce.py --fresh --jobs 2 . Reproduce Use Lean 4.34.1 , with Mathlib pinned to d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612 . Extract the source archive and run from its package root: lake exe cache get python3 scripts/source_manifest.py --check python3 reproduce.py --fresh --jobs 2 The source archive contains all 942 pinned proof/tool/data files, the exact certificates, deterministic generators, a paper-to-Lean proof map, and verification scripts. The verification archive retains literal logs, source hashes, root/axiom inventories, component provenance, and the original full CI artifact. RELEASE_MANIFEST.json binds both archives to the verified and published sources; SHA256SUMS gives transport hashes. Scope and preserved history This release completes the specified purity theorem for all n >= 3. It does not claim a classification of all maximizers, arbitrary first-factor dimension, a separability optimum, novelty/priority, or external peer review. The physical necessity and direct attainment proofs avoid assuming a full Hildebrand if-and-only-if theorem. The immutable appt-qutrit-purity-interim-v1 Release and its source tree/assets are unchanged. Earlier failed audit attempts are retained as failed records, not relabeled as successes.
title: mxym/math: Qutrit–qudit APPT purity: complete all-n Lean proof v1

summary: DSM–861 is best understood as a deterministic spectral computing architecture built from a rigid finite graph, a toroidal Hodge geometry, nonlinear KAN transport, vorton-inspired skew coupling, and associative-memory snapping. The arithmetic anchor is 861 = 42,2= T41 = 3 · 7 · 41,  while the interaction topology is exactly J(42, 2) with degree 80 and spectrum {80, 38, −2}. The toroidal layer supplies a genuine discrete differential calculus. The finite-state theorem fixes the exact nine-qubit boundary of a single 861-dimensional core. The controllability theorem converts universal computation into a concrete Lie-algebra calculation. The snapping theorem supplies a mathematically correct route to non-accumulating numerical error through a deliberately constructed quadratic attractor. The resulting program is therefore executable as mathematics and engineering. Build the graph. Build the Hodge operators. Construct the control generators. Compute their Lie closure. Implement the nonlinear snap. Measure the ϵ2 law. Synthesize the FPGA. Then benchmark complete circuits. If those tests succeed, DSM–861 becomes a demonstrated deterministic spectral processor rather than merely a conceptual analogy to quantum computing.
title: Deterministic Spectral Quantum Emulation on Classical Hardware

summary: Replication package for a validation study of three off-the-shelf sentiment instruments (SenticNet 9, VADER, Twitter-RoBERTa) against blind three-coder human annotation on a stratified audit sample of 504 tweets, drawn from a collection of English-language tweets directed at six European airlines in the summers of 2018-2022 (252,650 user tweets after removal of re-captured records). The package contains, with no tweet text: tweet-level labels of all three instruments for every collected record (re-captured records and truncated author identifiers flagged); the 504 audited items with all three coders' original ratings, the original majority consensus, the post-audit adjudications and completed ratings, and a text-free linkage summary of each audited item's capture multiplicity; the codebook; the VADER and Twitter-RoBERTa scorers with the model revision; a conda environment manifest; and a single script (code/reproduce_all.py) that regenerates every statistic in the manuscript's tables, including the multiplicity-adjusted stratified difference estimates. See README.md for the layout, the sampling note, and the reproducibility boundaries (the historical SenticNet API run cannot be re-executed; the corpus cannot be rehydrated because platform identifiers were truncated at collection).
title: Replication package: Sentiment Instruments Are Not Interchangeable — Audited Validity, Its Descriptive Consequences, and Its Correction in Airline-Directed Twitter Discourse

summary: A customer attempts an online booking, receives no confirmation, and finds that the support form requires a booking number that was never issued. No one has rejected the claim; the procedure cannot even receive it. This paper argues that such failures are not merely problems of customer service. They raise a question of justice. When a business controls the ordinary route through which consumers assert contractual rights, it bears responsibility for the avoidable and disproportionate burdens created by that route. The paper calls this principle procedural responsibility . Survey data show that the anticipated effort of complaining is a common reason for doing nothing. Among consumers who experienced a problem but took no action, 57 percent expected complaining to take too long and 43 percent expected it to be too complicated (Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025). European and German law address parts of this problem, and Spain's 2025 customer-support law demonstrates that legislators can establish specific procedural duties. Yet a coherent cross-sector standard for accessible, traceable and substantive complaint handling remains missing in EU and German law. The paper proposes five rights: reciprocal communication, a continuing case record, human reconsideration of unresolved claims, timely handling of urgent matters, and access to relevant evidence. It also outlines proportionate remedies for objectively established procedural failures that do not require another exhausting complaint. The goal is not to guarantee that consumers win disputes, but to ensure that their claims can be received, examined and meaningfully decided. The principle applies from letters and call centres to chatbots and AI agents, offering a concrete direction for the European Commission's planned Digital Fairness Act.
title: The Cost of Having Rights: Why a Consumer Complaint Is a Question of Justice, Not Customer Service

summary: daf-jev 0.7.2 provides typed native decision clients, provider-neutral backends, pure composition, exact discrete graphical inference, independently labeled dataset preparation, frozen benchmark protocols, decimal cost accounting, and reproducible manuscript evidence. This release adds an explicitly bounded native OpenRouter execution contract for TypeSafe Jev, a separately defined Perplexity Decisions contract, and prospective interleaved native-model comparison protocols. The selected native hosted evidence contains 12 successful capability calls, including complete 77-way BANKING77 and 151-way CLINC option vocabularies, with reported billing of USD 0.000556920. These capability checks establish endpoint and task support; they do not establish dataset accuracy or calibrated probability meaning. Larger native hosted studies are ongoing and remain outside this release's completed research claims. Historical unknown billing and partial local results remain explicitly identified. Two native Mac Python profiles passed all 2,436 unit cases with combined coverage above 92%; package and manuscript reproduction were independently reviewed. The seven release assets contain the source, wheel, sdist, 30-page manuscript, selected evidence archive, release manifest, and checksums. Historical synthetic security-test canaries are retained as fixtures; real credentials, private journals, model weights, and raw corpora are excluded. Source build, artifact, and main commit identities are recorded separately in the release manifest.
title: daf-jev: Modular Decision Models, Orchestration, and Reproducible Evaluation

summary: DATASET OVERVIEW This repository contains the synthetic satellite constellation scheduling datasets generated by the KEPLER Data Factory (KDF). As detailed in the KDF framework paper, these datasets bridge the semantic gap between human strategic intent and low-level system execution by combining deterministic orbital physics with semantic text generation. The data is organized into two main versions (v2 and v3), which contain the experimental scenarios evaluated across different Large Language Models (LLMs) to assess semantic fidelity in translating operational constraints. VERSION 2 (v2) - BASELINE CONFIGURATION This directory contains the initial configuration datasets evaluated across 5 different LLM architectures (Gemma 2, LLaMA 3.1, Phi-3.5, Phi-4, and Qwen2) as discussed in the paper's results section. The baseline simulation parameters are structured as follows: • Scenarios: 25 • Satellites: 5 • Ground Stations: 2 • Tasks per Scenario: 15 • Random Seed: 2026 • Temporal Prompting Logic: Instructs the LLM to interpret timeframes using a single fluid, human-centric relative phrasing that fuses the macro day and local diurnal hour (e.g., tomorrow morning) without utilizing raw countdown metrics, reflecting the framework's goal of natural language domain translation. VERSION 3 (v3) - SCALED CONFIGURATION This directory contains larger dataset configurations designed to evaluate higher-capacity models (LLaMA 3.1:8b, Phi-4:14b, and Gemma 2:27b) under a heavier operational workload, as explored in the scaling evaluation phase of the paper. The scaled simulation parameters include: • Scenarios: 50 • Satellites: 8 • Ground Stations: 3 • Tasks per Scenario: 40 • Random Seed: 0 • Temporal Prompting Logic: Updates the temporal generation rules to explicitly frame the timeframes as strict operational delivery deadlines, enforcing phrasing that marks the absolute limit for data availability based on a target day and diurnal period. INTERNAL SCENARIO STRUCTURE As described in the "The KEPLER Data Factory" section of the paper, the framework operates through a sequential pipeline (Data Collector, Physics Engine, and Request Generator) managed by a main orchestrator. Inside each LLM's dataset directory, there is a configuration file (config.yaml) detailing the specific simulation variables. Consequently, the execution of the pipeline yields the following core components inside each individual scenario folder (e.g., scenario_1): • scenario_report.json: A report outputted by the Data Collector detailing the generated entities (ground stations and satellites) and their physical characteristics, such as locations, payloads, and communication bands. • physics_passes_report.json: A report outputted by the Physics Engine containing the deterministically calculated communication and contact windows (using SGP4 and Skyfield), alongside their associated times and locations. • ollama_prompt_TASK_GEN_[...].txt: Individual text files containing the domain-translated system prompts and enriched structured variables sent to the LLM Request Generator to guide the operational request generation process. • ollama_prompts_combined.json: The final integrated dataset file containing the compiled prompts, the generated natural language requests, and the computed semantic validation metrics (cosine similarity scores) for the scenario.   The complete source code for the KEPLER Data Factory (KDF) framework, along with detailed documentation, methodology, and instructions for generating custom datasets, is publicly available. You can access the KDF project repository, architecture details, and supplementary materials at: https://thesoftwaredesignlab.github.io/KEPLER-DF/index.html

summary: MANIFESTO MSDT ( Metodo Scientifico Digitale Tola ). Il presente documento e' un quadro olistico operativo a norma di legge  per la gestione della proprietà intellettuale e la validazione crittografica delle competenze educative e scientifiche. FRAMEWORK  EUROPEO MSDT - Medoto Scientifico Digitale Tola Autorità Internazionale IANA PEN: Integrazione strutturale del Private Enterprise Number 66881 , assegnato dall'Internet Assigned Numbers Authority. La radice OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.66881 funge da nodo gerarchico primario da cui dipendono i moduli di interblocco macchina e supervisione umana.   DESCRIZIONE Italiano (Riepilogo esecutivo per la conformità all'AI Act): Questo documento aggiornato integra il Riepilogo esecutivo della metodologia MSDT (Metodo Scientifico Digitale Tola). Definisce un quadro sovrano per la ricerca scientifica indipendente e la supervisione umana dei sistemi di IA, in piena conformità con l'AI Act dell'UE (Regolamento UE 2024/1689). La metodologia MSDT utilizza: Notarizzazione crittografica: Prova temporale immutabile tramite Bitcoin Blockchain (OpenTimestamps). Validazione istituzionale: Protocolli depositati presso MIMIT, CNR e l'Autorità Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Garante della privacy). Elaborazione cognitiva ad alta frequenza: Esecuzione documentata di 176 ore di formazione specialistica PNRR. Vigilanza UE sull'IA: Monitoraggio attivo dei progetti open source su code.europa.eu per il Garante europeo della protezione dei dati (EDPS). summary: Data and code underlying the manuscript "Sub-diffraction confinement of the optical magnetic field, and the fixed-plane reference that overstates its loss with depth" (Optics Express, submitted). An azimuthally polarized beam focused by a flat concentric-ring silicon-nanopillar metasurface produces a focal spot whose on-axis field is purely magnetic. This deposit contains the optimization records, full-wave field data, meta-atom library and analysis code behind every figure and every quoted number in that manuscript. Fixed parameters: wavelength 1.55 um, aperture radius 31.0 um, focal length 15.5 um (NA 0.8944; a second aperture at NA 0.7105), 20 rings of minimum width 3 cells, cell pitch 0.50 um, pillar height 1.15 um. Contents (210 files, 49.9 MB unpacked): per-point genetic-optimizer records for the single-plane, soft-penalty, depth-window and convergence runs; axial scans and depth reference tables; fabrication Monte Carlo and illumination sensitivity data; cylindrical and three-dimensional full wave field data; the meta-atom library and its monotone inversion; the seven manuscript figures; and the propagation, mask, optimization and analysis scripts. Two notes for reusers, both expanded in README.md. First, the thin-annulus diffraction floor quoted for the focal plane is valid at z = f only; depth comparisons must be made plane by plane against the annulus at the same z, and the tables to do that are included. Second, four files contain rows produced before a defect in the magnetic figure of merit was fixed; they are retained so the defect is reproducible, each carries a comment header, and RETRACTIONS.md lists them. README.md, MANIFEST.csv (SHA-256 per file) and RETRACTIONS.md are uploaded both inside the archive and as separate files so they can be read from this page without downloading.
