summary: Orthonym is a deterministic, rule-based engine that names a molecular structure (SMILES) following the IUPAC 2013 recommendations, aiming at the Preferred IUPAC Name; the same input always gives the same output. Before a name is returned, OPSIN reads it back and the structure it reads is compared with the input; a candidate that fails is withdrawn. A few names OPSIN cannot read in full (names from exact-match lists, a few name forms outside OPSIN's grammar, and stereodescriptors OPSIN cannot parse) are returned by the default tier without that full read-back and are marked in the provenance output. Every name carries a tier label that says whether the engine certifies it as the Preferred IUPAC Name. Release notes: https://github.com/Steinbeck-Lab/Orthonym/releases/tag/v1.0.6
title: Orthonym

summary: A customer attempts an online booking, receives no confirmation, and finds that the support form requires a booking number that was never issued. No one has rejected the claim; the procedure cannot even receive it. This paper argues that such failures are not merely problems of customer service. They raise a question of justice. When a business controls the ordinary route through which consumers assert contractual rights, it bears responsibility for the avoidable and disproportionate burdens created by that route. The paper calls this principle procedural responsibility . Survey data show that the anticipated effort of complaining is a common reason for doing nothing. Among consumers who experienced a problem but took no action, 57 percent expected complaining to take too long and 43 percent expected it to be too complicated (Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025). European and German law address parts of this problem, and Spain's 2025 customer-support law demonstrates that legislators can establish specific procedural duties. Yet a coherent cross-sector standard for accessible, traceable and substantive complaint handling remains missing in EU and German law. The paper proposes five rights: reciprocal communication, a continuing case record, human reconsideration of unresolved claims, timely handling of urgent matters, and access to relevant evidence. It also outlines proportionate remedies for objectively established procedural failures that do not require another exhausting complaint. The goal is not to guarantee that consumers win disputes, but to ensure that their claims can be received, examined and meaningfully decided. The principle applies from letters and call centres to chatbots and AI agents, offering a concrete direction for the European Commission's planned Digital Fairness Act.
title: The Cost of Having Rights: Why a Consumer Complaint Is a Question of Justice, Not Customer Service

summary: Data and code underlying the manuscript "Sub-diffraction confinement of the optical magnetic field, and the fixed-plane reference that overstates its loss with depth" (Optics Express, submitted). An azimuthally polarized beam focused by a flat concentric-ring silicon-nanopillar metasurface produces a focal spot whose on-axis field is purely magnetic. This deposit contains the optimization records, full-wave field data, meta-atom library and analysis code behind every figure and every quoted number in that manuscript. Fixed parameters: wavelength 1.55 um, aperture radius 31.0 um, focal length 15.5 um (NA 0.8944; a second aperture at NA 0.7105), 20 rings of minimum width 3 cells, cell pitch 0.50 um, pillar height 1.15 um. Contents (210 files, 49.9 MB unpacked): per-point genetic-optimizer records for the single-plane, soft-penalty, depth-window and convergence runs; axial scans and depth reference tables; fabrication Monte Carlo and illumination sensitivity data; cylindrical and three-dimensional full wave field data; the meta-atom library and its monotone inversion; the seven manuscript figures; and the propagation, mask, optimization and analysis scripts. Two notes for reusers, both expanded in README.md. First, the thin-annulus diffraction floor quoted for the focal plane is valid at z = f only; depth comparisons must be made plane by plane against the annulus at the same z, and the tables to do that are included. Second, four files contain rows produced before a defect in the magnetic figure of merit was fixed; they are retained so the defect is reproducible, each carries a comment header, and RETRACTIONS.md lists them. README.md, MANIFEST.csv (SHA-256 per file) and RETRACTIONS.md are uploaded both inside the archive and as separate files so they can be read from this page without downloading.
title: Data and code for "Sub-diffraction confinement of the optical magnetic field, and the fixed-plane reference that overstates its loss with depth"

summary: This dataset contains raw SnoCam image data from NASA EXPORTS deployments in the North Atlantic. The image processing pipeline incorporated background removal, binarization and measurement of particle properties. Prior to background subtraction, we masked out the edges of images and converted raw images from the RGB domain (red, green, and blue) to a grayscale image. We discarded the excessively bright images (mean brightness > 120 out of 255), caused by strong daylight interference. The background removal utilized a fast fourier transform (FFT), followed by a Gaussian mask with a standard deviation of 2. This Gaussian mask worked as a low-pass filter to retain the low-frequency background. Then the filtered frequency-domain image was transformed back into the background image using inverse FFT. We then subtracted the background from the raw grayscale image. The subsequent step of binarization filtered out brightest regions using a threshold of mean pixel intensities plus five standard deviations. This step isolated potential particles called as markers, as pixels that passed the high threshold could represent cores of the particles. We took one additional step to identify particle boundaries by applying the Canny edge detection algorithm (Canny, 1986). We classified particles that failed both the edge detection and the brightness threshold as out-of-focus ones and eliminated them. The method of using markers and edge detection increased the robustness of particle identification and enhanced particle segmentation. The measured properties included area, major and minor axis lengths, equivalent spherical diameter (ESD), perimeter, the smallest bounding box. https://github.com/cadurkin/SnowCam/blob/60311eb98a70febbb3b93e64522d7ba704ccd7bf/SnowCam_Image_Analysis_EXPORTS2.ipynb
title: SnoCam V0 datasets from EXPORTS NA

summary: Choptuik's spacetime, the discretely self-similar solution at the threshold of black hole formation in the collapse of a massless scalar field, is expected to have exactly one unstable mode, whose growth rate λ determines the critical exponent γ = 1/λ ≈ 0.374. The existence of this spacetime was proved by Reiterer and Trubowitz with a computer-assisted argument. We prove, also with computer assistance, that in their realization the solution has exactly one unstable mode, modulo gauge, under spherically symmetric linear perturbations that are smooth in time and analytic in the radial variable up to and across the light cone. The mode is real and simple, with λ ∈ [2.674040, 2.674115], so that 1/λ ∈ [0.373955, 0.373966]. More precisely, per Floquet class the linearized operator has exactly four roots with positive real part: a gauge mode, which translates the time of the singularity; two roots whose eigenvectors violate the constraints; and the physical mode. The count uses an operator version of Rouché's theorem with a finite-dimensional reference, a rank-two deflation of the gauge roots, Newton–Kantorovich enclosures, and bounds in rational and ball arithmetic. The passage from the geometric problem to the operator rests on a global completeness result for the gauge and an explicit reconstruction of the perturbations. The certificates, a verification program and the data are publicly available. Resumo (português). O espaço-tempo de Choptuik, a solução discretamente autossimilar no limiar de formação de buraco negro no colapso de um campo escalar sem massa, deve ter exatamente um modo instável, cuja taxa de crescimento λ determina o expoente crítico γ = 1/λ ≈ 0.374. A existência desse espaço-tempo foi provada por Reiterer e Trubowitz com um argumento assistido por computador. Provamos, também com assistência computacional, que na realização deles a solução tem exatamente um modo instável, módulo gauge, sob perturbações lineares esfericamente simétricas que são suaves no tempo e analíticas na variável radial até o cone de luz e através dele. O modo é real e simples, com λ ∈ [2.674040, 2.674115], de modo que 1/λ ∈ [0.373955, 0.373966]. Mais precisamente, por classe de Floquet, o operador linearizado tem exatamente quatro raízes com parte real positiva: um modo de gauge, que translada o instante da singularidade; duas raízes cujos autovetores violam os vínculos; e o modo físico. A contagem usa uma versão para operadores do teorema de Rouché com uma referência de dimensão finita, uma deflação de posto dois das raízes de gauge, localizações rigorosas por Newton–Kantorovich e cotas em aritmética racional e de bolas. A passagem do problema geométrico ao operador se apoia num resultado de completude global do gauge e numa reconstrução explícita das perturbações. Os certificados, um programa de verificação e os dados estão disponíveis publicamente. Version 2 (October 2026). summary: Source code for Skillarum: Conditionally Reproducible Website-to-Agent-Skill Compilation. Release 0.3.1 is a correction release: math4wisdom-cube 0.3.0 withdraws an investigator claim that 0.2.0 adopted without recomputation (1+3+3+1 is not the generic grading pattern) and adds a check for the corrected statement; the changelog's account of investigator independence and two documentation statements are corrected.

summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code. Of 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,670 were used in another study and excluded from this analysis. Seventeen were excluded because their deposited assemblies did not meet the input criteria and raw-read download attempts were unsuccessful. The historical analyzable-input manifest therefore contained 42,591 records (40,094 public assemblies and 2,497 raw-derived inputs). Species adjudication excluded one record from each source, leaving 42,589 genomes: 40,093 public assemblies and 2,496 raw-derived genomes. Thirteen failed or unfinished raw-read attempts were retained through the public-assembly pathway and are not included in the 1,687 exclusions. Version 1.5.0 adds BioProject mapping for all 42,589 final genomes across 340 projects, descriptive project-level sensitivity analyses, updated record-disposition tables, and revised Figure 1 and Figure S1 materials. The locked primary cohort and primary statistical results remain unchanged. Exact-category sensitivity endpoints differ from the grouped primary endpoints; equal-project-weighted analyses and project bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Genome assemblies and raw reads were retrieved using a combination of scripts, download utilities, and manual downloads from repository webpages. Deposited assemblies were assessed first, with raw-read reconstruction attempted when a deposited assembly could not be retrieved or did not meet the input criteria. Exact historical read preprocessing commands could not be recovered. Adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are outside this deposit’s reproducibility claim. Record-level logs documenting the 17 exclusions were unavailable. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Retrieve sequence data from the original repositories using the supplied accession identifiers. Archived code supports the post-assembly cohort checks, primary statistical summaries, and BioProject sensitivity analyses. Jianhua Li and Jing Guo contributed equally. Jing Chen is the corresponding author (dongqingfei@126.com). summary: This article proposes Human Value Provenance (HVP) as a framework for identifying, measuring and valuing expert human-knowledge contributions in generative-AI co-creation. The approach distinguishes authorship, informational contribution and contribution to value, and develops the Human Contribution to AI Value (HCAV) instrument across eight dimensions: knowledge, originality, correction, judgment, connection, transformation, substitutability and value. The design combines longitudinal episode reconstruction, multidimensional coding, blinded external evaluation and AI-only counterfactuals. Pilot case HCAV-01 comprises 25 episodes and a preliminary estimate of 68 equivalent hours of expert contribution. Valuation is organized into three layers: V1, replacement cost of expertise; V2, incremental transformation value; and V3, realized value. The proposal seeks to determine whether identifiable human interventions produce measurable transformations in AI-assisted outcomes and whether that traceability can, in later research, support discussions of recognition, bargaining and individual or collective participation in generated value.

summary: A small training residual does not tell a physics-informed neural network when it is safe to stop. Repeatedly checking ordinary confidence intervals introduces an additional difficulty: the reported guarantee can fail precisely because it determines the stopping time. We develop interval-assisted error certificates that remain valid across adaptively selected network checkpoints and arbitrary audit stopping times. Continuous-domain residual enclosures provide a lower-envelope control variate and a sampling distribution that minimizes the worst-case range of importance-weighted observations. A bounded-mean betting process then controls the remaining integration uncertainty, while PDE stability translates the residual certificate into a solution-error bound. The resulting guarantee separates adaptive training from fresh, sequential auditing without requiring a fixed training horizon. Experiments comprise 80 fully trained networks, four manufactured elliptic and parabolic problems, two architectures, two training samplers, and 400 checkpoint audits. At an absolute L2 tolerance of 0.01, the method certifies 79 of 80 trajectories, compared with 77 for corrected empirical-Bernstein bounds and 61 for corrected Hoeffding bounds. On the two-dimensional Poisson problem, these counts are 20, 18, and 2. Interval-guided sampling improves audit efficiency, but complete certification is not free: the median replayed total cost is 1.73 times full training. These findings establish a practical distinction between obtaining an accurate neural solution and having statistically valid evidence to stop computing it.
title: When to Stop Physics-Informed Learning

summary: This replication package contains the analytical data, R code, intermediate outputs, robustness diagnostics, figures, and documentation supporting the study “When Twin Transitions Compete: AI Acceleration, Digital Absorptive Capacity, and Renewable-Capacity Expansion in the European Union.” The study examines the EU-27 over 2015–2025 and evaluates whether economies with greater predetermined digital absorptive capacity experienced different renewable-capacity trajectories during the post-2022 acceleration in artificial intelligence. The package supports reproduction of the principal two-way fixed-effects models, event-study estimates, post-2022 differential-exposure specifications, placebo tests, alternative exposure and outcome models, mechanism tests, leave-one-country-out analysis, geopolitical sensitivity tests, and wild-cluster-bootstrap inference.

summary: A customer attempts an online booking, receives no confirmation, and finds that the support form requires a booking number that was never issued. No one has rejected the claim; the procedure cannot even receive it. This paper argues that such failures are not merely problems of customer service. They raise a question of justice. When a business controls the ordinary route through which consumers assert contractual rights, it bears responsibility for the avoidable and disproportionate burdens created by that route. The paper calls this principle procedural responsibility . Survey data show that the anticipated effort of complaining is a common reason for doing nothing. Among consumers who experienced a problem but took no action, 57 percent expected complaining to take too long and 43 percent expected it to be too complicated (Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025). European and German law address parts of this problem, and Spain's 2025 customer-support law demonstrates that legislators can establish specific procedural duties. Yet a coherent cross-sector standard for accessible, traceable and substantive complaint handling remains missing in EU and German law. The paper proposes five rights: reciprocal communication, a continuing case record, human reconsideration of unresolved claims, timely handling of urgent matters, and access to relevant evidence. It also outlines proportionate remedies for objectively established procedural failures that do not require another exhausting complaint. The goal is not to guarantee that consumers win disputes, but to ensure that their claims can be received, examined and meaningfully decided. The principle applies from letters and call centres to chatbots and AI agents, offering a concrete direction for the European Commission's planned Digital Fairness Act.
title: The Cost of Having Rights: Why a Consumer Complaint Is a Question of Justice, Not Customer Service

summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code. Of 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,670 were used in another study and excluded from this analysis. Seventeen were excluded because their deposited assemblies did not meet the input criteria and raw-read download attempts were unsuccessful. The historical analyzable-input manifest therefore contained 42,591 records (40,094 public assemblies and 2,497 raw-derived inputs). Species adjudication excluded one record from each source, leaving 42,589 genomes: 40,093 public assemblies and 2,496 raw-derived genomes. Thirteen failed or unfinished raw-read attempts were retained through the public-assembly pathway and are not included in the 1,687 exclusions. Version 1.5.0 adds BioProject mapping for all 42,589 final genomes across 340 projects, descriptive project-level sensitivity analyses, updated record-disposition tables, and revised Figure 1 and Figure S1 materials. The locked primary cohort and primary statistical results remain unchanged. Exact-category sensitivity endpoints differ from the grouped primary endpoints; equal-project-weighted analyses and project bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Genome assemblies and raw reads were retrieved using a combination of scripts, download utilities, and manual downloads from repository webpages. Deposited assemblies were assessed first, with raw-read reconstruction attempted when a deposited assembly could not be retrieved or did not meet the input criteria. Exact historical read preprocessing commands could not be recovered. Adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are outside this deposit’s reproducibility claim. Record-level logs documenting the 17 exclusions were unavailable. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Retrieve sequence data from the original repositories using the supplied accession identifiers. Archived code supports the post-assembly cohort checks, primary statistical summaries, and BioProject sensitivity analyses. Jianhua Li and Jing Guo contributed equally. Jing Chen is the corresponding author (dongqingfei@126.com). Funding: Natural Science Foundation of Xiamen Municipality (3502Z202373092) and Xiamen Medical and Health Guidance Project (3502Z20254ZD1079).

summary: This paper presents a diagnostic theory that interprets a phenomenon observed in advanced economies—monetary easing and standard macroeconomic policies no longer generating sustained growth, even as they are accompanied by improvements in employment—not as a "failure of policy management" or a temporary demand shortfall, but as the structural depletion of investment outlets. As its core concepts, this paper introduces the structural frontier coefficient Φ, which represents the latent constraint determined by demographics, the institutional environment, and capital structure, and the critical threshold θ, at which policy effects undergo a qualitative shift. It further presents the "demand-constrained growth hypothesis" as the mechanism through which the structural frontier becomes constraining as the economy matures. The paper divides demand-side constraints into four types of goods—time-constrained goods, goods with strong ownership constraints, goods with weak ownership constraints and multiple ownership, and conduit goods—and organizes demand displacement and qualitative-improvement constraints as cross-cutting constraints superimposed on them. In an economy whose room for quantitative expansion has shrunk, the center of growth shifts to qualitative improvement; however, as the quality frontier is approached, the marginal cost of improvement rises while marginal utility and the scope for price pass-through may decline, so that technological progress may diverge from growth in sales and GDP. In the region Φ > θ, Solow-type growth theory and New Keynesian transmission may, by and large, function effectively, whereas in the region Φ ≤ θ, the spillover of monetary easing to real investment and sustained growth weakens, and easing tends instead to spill over into alternative channels such as asset prices, fund retention, and external capital movements. On the other hand, because the sensitivity of the employment channel to Φ is relatively lower than that of the growth channel, employment responses may remain relatively intact even in the region Φ ≤ θ. This asymmetry of the dual channels explains the simultaneous occurrence of employment improvement and growth stagnation. Under the definitional constraint that Φ is not back-calculated from outcome variables, this paper presents a two-layer diagnostic identification procedure. The structural state is diagnosed from the component-wise directions (structural signature) of the ordinal scale Φ̂, which is constructed without using outcome variables, and from the binding constraint; the policy transmission state is classified separately by the responses of the growth and alternative channels to identified monetary policy shocks (employment responses are checked as an auxiliary diagnosis); the two are then compared, with the estimate a of the realized investment ratio α, the cost-push coefficient κ, and other measures reported alongside as auxiliary findings. Furthermore, under the hypothesis that in mature, constrained regimes the elasticity of substitution declines and the dominant bottleneck determines the viability of investment, the paper positions the min approximation not as a predictive function but as a diagnostic limit. summary: Semantic framework for preparing scientific simulation scenarios, validating typed configurations and qualifying numerical outputs with explicit provenance. summary: This dataset supports a multicenter retrospective cohort study comparing long-term outcomes between neoadjuvant chemotherapy and adjuvant chemotherapy in women with operable HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer treated in China between 2013 and 2019. The dataset includes 2,355 patients, comprising 868 patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and 1,487 patients who received adjuvant chemotherapy. It contains deidentified patient-level clinicopathological characteristics, treatment information, clinical and pathological response variables, disease-free survival outcomes, and overall survival outcomes. Two data files are provided: analysis_data_unweighted_deidentified.xlsx contains the cleaned unweighted analysis cohort, and analysis_data_iptw_weighted_deidentified.csv contains the corresponding analysis dataset with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights targeting the average treatment effect. Direct patient identifiers have been removed. Because the files contain individual-level clinical data, access is restricted to protect patient privacy. Researchers requesting access should provide their name, institutional affiliation, research purpose, and proposed analysis plan. Approved users must not attempt to reidentify participants or redistribute the data. The study was approved by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University (approval number ZZ2024-273-02) and was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400083063).
title: Deidentified Data for Neoadjuvant versus Adjuvant Chemotherapy in HR Positive HER2 Negative Breast Cancer

summary: Background/Objectives: Fictional portrayals of criminal investigation have long inflated public expectations of forensic science, in a phenomenon known as the CSI effect. As artificial intelligence, data science and three-dimensional reconstruction enter operational policing, that distortion extends into what we term the Digital CSI effect. This study examines how narrative-driven, interactive science communication can recalibrate such expectations while building technological and ethical literacy among adult audiences. Methods: Using a descriptive multiple-case design, we examined four deliveries of two workshops involving 98 adult participants across three audience types: general public, law enforcement practitioners and trainees, and postgraduate students. Workshop 2 introduced artificial intelligence and 3D crime scene reconstruction in an immersive virtual environment. Four propositions were formulated before delivery and examined at each case against facilitator observation, question-and-answer sessions and open-ended written feedback. summary: Rationale. Implantation of permanent pacemakers in patients after repeat cardiac surgery can be significantly limited by cicatricial changes, recent cannulations, and obliteration of conventional venous accesses. An additional complication is the presence of congenital variants of systemic venous return, primarily persistent left superior vena cava (PSVC), which alters the geometry of endocardial electrode placement and increases the risk of technical complications. Case Description: This patient presented with a complex cardiac surgical history: aortic coarctation reconstruction in 2013, David I surgery in December 2025, and subsequent emergency hospitalization for decompensated chronic heart failure secondary to aortic valve avulsion and severe aortic regurgitation. On June 10, 2026, the patient underwent repeat aortic valve replacement with a Perceval L seamless biological valve prosthesis for life-saving reasons. In the early postoperative period, manifestations of sick sinus syndrome persisted, with transient second-degree sinoatrial block and pauses up to 3950 ms. Therefore, implantation of a dual-chamber, rate-adaptive pacemaker was planned for June 12, 2026. Intraoperatively, the standard right-sided approach was deemed unacceptable due to a fresh postoperative wound, severe tissue edema, and recent cannulation of the right subclavian artery. Upon conversion to the left subclavian approach, a stented septal vein (SVC) was detected with drainage through the dilated coronary sinus into the right atrium. Given preserved atrioventricular conduction, severe hypocoagulation, thrombocytopenia, and a high risk of coronary sinus injury, a decision was made to abandon the ventricular lead and perform single-chamber atrial pacing in AAIR mode. The lead with active fixation was successfully advanced through the splanchnic vein and the coronary sinus into the right atrium. Conclusion. This clinical observation demonstrates that in a patient with sick sinus syndrome and preserved atrioventricular conduction, AAIR mode can be a reasonable and technically safe option for permanent pacing when standard venous access is impossible and there is a high risk of ventricular lead placement through an anomalous venous collector.

summary: Abstract Accurate protein structure prediction does not necessarily identify the conformational state relevant to a specific biological or pharmacological function. In practice, structural biologists often resolve this ambiguity by drawing on homologous, family-related or ligand-bound reference structures, but this process remains largely heuristic and expert-dependent. Here we formalize such reference-guided structural reasoning as a quantitative framework for functional conformational modelling. Transition Diffusion Dynamics (TDD) learns reusable molecular-dynamics-derived structural transformation priors, whereas TDD-DE combines these priors with reference-supported structural information to model specified functional states. Across approximately 600 held-out proteins, TDD-DE improved ligand-pocket reconstruction from AlphaFold-derived structures while maintaining global fold agreement and outperformed molecular dynamics and representative generative conformational models at the pocket level. Prospective target-hidden applications in C3aR, rhodopsin, D2R and SIRT3 demonstrated that related structural references could be transferred to previously unresolved target states and support experimental discovery. These results move protein modelling beyond static structure prediction toward quantitative modelling of functionally relevant conformational states, providing a framework for linking structural prediction to mechanistic interpretation and structure-guided drug discovery.
title: Learning Protein Conformational Transitions for Reference-Guided Functional Conformational Modelling

summary: This archive contains scientific spectra and diagnostic products from atmospheric retrievals of the benchmark early-L dwarfs HD 89744B, GJ 1048B, and LSPM J0632+5053B. The Scientific_spectra.zip file contains the processed spectra of all three targets at their native instrumental resolutions, along with the spectra convolved to an effective resolving power of R<=100 used in the atmospheric retrievals presented in the paper. The retrievals compare models with and without gaseous SiO under cloud-free, gray cloud, and physical condensate cloud treatments. Additional silicate compositions are included for HD 89744B and GJ 1048B. Each retrieval directory contains posterior corner plots, spectral model comparisons and residuals, pressure-temperature profiles, molecular abundance profiles, effective-temperature posteriors, cloud profiles where applicable, and a parameter_summary.txt file.
title: Retrieval Diagnostic Products for "Gaseous SiO and Silicate Clouds in Three Benchmark Early-L Dwarfs"
